rhythm.value: Corrected: 67 shots, 66 cuts in 69.83 s (56.7 cuts/min), median hold 0.83 s, p10 0.067 s, p90 2.56 s. Detector: 58 shots, 57 cuts (49.0/min), median 0.77 s. The median is pulled down by one 1.87 s flurry of 23 images; without it, 44 cuts, median hold 1.40 s (p10 0.16, p90 2.68). Pace by section: hook 5.43 s single shot; heritage 5.43-16.57 s ten shots, four of them 4-frame archive steps; list 21.33-30.97 s holds about 1.0-1.47 s; questions 36.53-47.1 s holds 1.7-2.6 s; flurry 2-3 frames; proof 0.5-1.67 s; close 1.03, 1.83, 2.73, 3.2, 4.77 s, the longest holds of the film. I cannot hear the film: tempo confidence is 0.04 and cuts land on beats, onsets and loudness swells at or below chance (below), so the cutting follows the words and the images, not a beat grid. Corrected cuts (66): on a beat ±80 ms 0.197 against chance 0.272 (lift 0.72); on an onset 0.545 against 0.630; within one frame of a downbeat 0.015 against 0.032. Without the flurry (44 cuts): beats 0.159, onsets 0.477, loudness swells (50 ms RMS peaks over 1.35x median, 69 found) ±0.1 s 0.114 against 0.20. Per loudness section 7.8-44.8 s: beats 0.167 vs 0.298, onsets 0.542 vs 0.691; 47.35-63.74 s: beats 0.212 vs 0.296, onsets 0.606 vs 0.670. Detector figures in sync.json agree: 0.211 vs 0.273, onsets 0.509 vs 0.633, lift 0.77, downbeat-frame lift 0.6, signed median +0.035 s. Onsets run 4.5 a second, so the onset ratios say nothing either way. Whisper word ends fall on whole seconds a third of the time, so word times are too coarse to test cuts against; the observed rule is order, not timing: each listed word arrives on the same frame as its own image (23.30, 24.30 s).

value.name: archive-ladder-match-cut
value.description: Four images of one building, 4 frames each (F206, F210, F214, F218), each entered through a 1-2 frame grade or texture flash, then a match cut at F222 to the same building in present-day colour, held 4.77 s. Framing of the building stays in the same place across all five images.
value.why: At 4 frames per image the eye cannot read each photo, only that the same shape persists while its age changes; the long colour hold after 0.53 s of flicker lands the location as the answer and gives the caption time to type.

value.name: speed-ramp-flurry
value.description: 23 banknote images in 1.87 s on a 3-2-3-2 frame cadence (F1456, F1459, F1461, F1464 ... F1511), 12 images a second; the cadence is consistent with a 24 fps edit of 2-frame holds pulled down to 30 fps (inferred). Preceded by a 1.43 s still office hold and followed by a 1.67 s still tower hold. RMS over the flurry -13.6 dB against -15.8 dB in the 2.5 s before.
value.why: The flurry is the only fast passage in the film and it carries what the event rejects; the still holds either side make the burst read as noise to be cut away, and the eye registers only the subject, never a single note.

value.name: typewriter-backspace-hook
value.description: Small left-set serif line (x 0.18, line box 0.061 high) types on black from F4; a stack of archive portraits beside it changes every 5-6 frames until 1.26 s; at 3.73-4.10 s the line deletes backwards in word chunks (arrive, future, watching the, happen by, doesn't) one chunk every 2 frames (F114-F122); the first word slides right over F126-F129 and is hard-swapped to its replacement on F130; the rest of the counter-statement lands as spaced words.
value.why: Writing and then deleting a claim on screen tells the viewer the film disagrees with the obvious statement before a single image is shown; a black ground with one small line holds attention on the words for 5.4 s.

value.name: light-leak-flash-cut
value.description: Hard cuts between graded plates hide behind a 1-3 frame flash: overexposed warm frame then green-white leak (F363-F364) before the new plate at F365; the same family at 6.83-6.93 (texture overlay), 7.23-7.27, 16.43-16.53 (green grade and white flare), 22.26-22.33 (cyan, then white), 29.46-29.5 (navy flip, then white), 45.33-45.40 (navy, then beige).
value.why: A flash saturates the eye for a frame, so the jump between unrelated archive and stock plates is felt as one continuous film roll rather than a slideshow.

value.name: caused-morph
value.description: A small image card (0.11 of frame width, top right of a paper page, F886-F902) grows to full bleed over 9 frames (F903 0.18, F905 0.47, F907 0.88, F911 1.0 of width), the type staying put on the paper until covered; the same move on black at 27.23-27.40 s in three steps (F817, F819, F822).
value.why: The card is already in view while the line types, so the eye is parked on it; its growth turns a thumbnail into the next scene without a cut, which keeps the list feeling continuous.
